title: Seated Chair Exercises: For Bigger Bodies or Painful Joints
intro: Yes, you can exercise while sitting on a chair and it still benefits you. These exercises suit bigger bodies, painful knees or lower back, or anyone just starting out.
muscles: Front thighs, calves, hips, shoulders, arms and stomach muscles (core). It also helps your heart work a little harder without loading your joints.
steps: Choose a sturdy chair without wheels. Sit at the edge of the chair, feet flat on the floor, back upright.
Seated marching: lift your left and right knees alternately for 30 seconds. Swing your arms too.
Leg straightening: lift one leg until straight, hold 2 seconds, lower slowly. Do 8 times each leg.
Forward punches: punch forward with alternating arms for 30 seconds. Keep shoulders relaxed, don't lift them to your ears.
Arm raises: lift both arms as high as is comfortable, lower slowly. Do 8 times.
Rest 30 seconds, then repeat the round. Breathe normally throughout.
mistakes: Slouching until your back aches. Sit upright, imagine your head being pulled up to the ceiling.
Going too fast until you lose control. Slow, controlled moves are safer and more effective.
Holding your breath during the moves. Breathe out when lifting, breathe in when lowering.
easier: Cut the time to 15-20 seconds per move and rest longer. You can also lift your leg only halfway, within a pain-free range.
harder: Increase to 45 seconds per move, or hold a 500ml water bottle during arm moves. Once comfortable, try standing up from the chair and sitting back down slowly.
dose: Start with 2 rounds (about 5-8 minutes), 3-5 times a week. When it feels easy, increase to 3 rounds.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain, chest pain, dizziness or unusual shortness of breath. If you recently had surgery or an injury, see a doctor or physiotherapist first before starting.

faq.a: Yes, for beginners it's a very good step. It builds basic strength and stamina. To lose weight, combine it with eating suitable portions, because fat loss comes from your overall eating and movement.

faq.q: Can I do these exercises at the office?
faq.a: Yes. Seated marching and leg straightening can be done under your desk. Try doing 2-3 minutes every 1-2 hours, while taking a break from your screen.

faq.q: How long before I can do standing exercises?
faq.a: There's no fixed timeline, it depends on your body. When 3 rounds feel easy and there's no pain, you can try standing moves while holding a chair.
